analysis:
Reviewed the two head_text units of docs/reference/protocol-messages.md (lines 326-947). The PR is documentation-only: it bumps the date, adds an "Add-on hold busy fields" section (busy_reason, busy_since_ms, busy_addon), and adds a heartbeat row at line 383. It also changes a few unseen ranges, at head lines 284 and 1445. No code or control changes are visible, so I found no concrete security regression.

Security-relevant observations for later passes:
- The new busy_* heartbeat fields are provider-supplied. `busy_addon` is a code-signing identifier or `operator`, and it is untrusted free text from the provider (ADV-001). The coordinator's bounds, length caps and sanitization for it are outside the supplied evidence. Draining status excludes the provider from routing (line 371), so a provider can self-exclude. That is not a privilege gain, only an availability effect on itself.
- The docs state the hold never sends `provider_drain` and returns on the same connection via an idle or serving heartbeat. Whether App Attest serving authorization (TB-011, T-053) and the per-connection grant remain bound across the hold depends on the platform-owned implementation, which is not supplied. Nothing visible weakens grant revocation.
- The remaining retained content (prefix-cache objects, ready_boundary_mode, telemetry, service reservation correlation, inference_error sanitization) looks like unchanged context. The cache fields reference T-041, whose mitigations (HMAC names, 30-minute TTL, account-scoped salt) are not altered by what is visible. I did not see the patch for the earlier ranges (lines 171-195 beyond the excerpt, 284, 1445), so coverage of those is limited.
- The new section's claim that the Swift encoder emits busy fields only beside draining is a documentation claim. The actual code (CoordinatorClient+Registration.swift, ProviderBusy.swift) was not supplied, so it is unverified.

No threat-model update appears required beyond the possible note that busy_addon is untrusted telemetry.
